headline: Google's first data center satellite is online and writing poetry
summary: The Suncatcher satellite, carrying a Google TPU, has successfully communicated with Earth and generated AI-powered poetry.
details: Google's prototype Suncatcher satellite, equipped with a single Google Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) and capable of generating up to 1 kW of electricity, is now online and communicating with ground control. Launched earlier this month on a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, this satellite is a precursor to future networks of orbiting data centers designed for large inference workloads.

After a three-week commissioning period, the satellite successfully received its first prompt: to have the pre-loaded Google DeepMind Gemma 4 model write a haiku about being in space. The AI responded with: 'Blue marble below / Data streams in silent grace / Starlight feeds my core.' The satellite also reported on its orbital conditions.

The ongoing test campaign will rigorously examine the TPU's performance under thermal stress and the harsh space radiation environment. While Google has conducted extensive ground testing in particle accelerators, this mission will assess the real-world effects of radiation, which can cause 'bit flips' and data corruption.

If the current TPU proves capable, Google plans to launch two more satellites in 2027. These future spacecraft will feature higher power generation and demonstrate inter-satellite optical links, a key component for supporting coherent distributed workloads in space.

Google's Starcloud project aims to create a constellation of satellites capable of performing inference loads individually, with high-speed links between them. This vision is closely tied to SpaceX, with Alphabet (Google's parent company) holding a significant investment in SpaceX and both companies relying on SpaceX's Starship for future launches.
